BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Harbourglass Seller Documents Against Buyer Playbook

## Scope and a procedural point

The Seller's note asks us to treat clauses marked [STANDARD] as "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and to focus only on [OPEN] items. I have not done that. Nothing in our playbook records agreement to the Seller's package, and almost every [STANDARD] item departs from our positions. Its labels do not bind the Buyer. I have reviewed every item, including the Disclosure Letter. Please don't let the "accepted framework" language carry into the mark-up.

## Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Buyer playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m start; 20% only with written AF authority, none given | Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not offer 20%. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Counter at AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery. |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with AF written approval, none given | Counter at 24 months. |
| Title/capacity regime | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. This is a material departure. |
| Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable | Reject. Add the fraud carve-out. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | General disclosure of the whole data room and public registers | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Delete. |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent satisfied on delivery of written consent | Effective consent plus evidence conditions are met before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject. |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | Release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and AF approval | Reject. |
| Employee bonuses / funds flow | AUD 420,000 excluded from funds flow, "a matter for the Seller" | Must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them | Reject. |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure | Reject. |
| DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand; preserve logs, investigate, require updates | Reject the materiality characterisation as well as any assumption of breach. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Reject the characterisation. Assess the contracts. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Reject. Keep Tax and IP separate from the general regime. |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is an internal source | Reject as sufficient. |

## Reasoning on the material issues

**1. The limitation package is the largest exposure.** The Seller's package moves the cap down by AUD 1.2m, lifts the de minimis fivefold and the basket fivefold, converts the basket to excess-only recovery, and shortens the time limit by six months. Taken together, a claim of AUD 240,000 would be fully excluded under the basket structure, and recovery on larger claims would be reduced by up to AUD 250,000 before the cap applies. The Seller's position is therefore not a modest adjustment. The 20% cap and 18-month period can be offered only if Amelia Frost gives written approval identifying the draft, and no such approval has been given.

**2. Title and fundamental warranties.** Putting title and capacity under the general caps and time limits would expose the Buyer to losses on the very matters it is buying. Title needs its own regime (100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket and de minimis). Independent evidence is also required. The DD-012 share register is a Seller-supplied record and does not show that the Buyer has verified title or encumbrances.

**3. Fraud carve-out.** The Seller's blanket application of limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" would cover fraud. Our playbook requires the carve-out to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive it.

**4. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Disclosure of the whole data room and public registers, combined with the knowledge exclusion, would require the Buyer to have found and understood every document in the room. Those two provisions together would remove most warranty claims. Both need to be replaced with specific fair disclosure, and the knowledge exclusion should be deleted.

**5. Bluefen (about 30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller has not provided a final consent, and DL 2 confirms this. "Consent satisfied on delivery" is consent-on-delivery, not a condition. The Buyer needs effective written consent and evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are met before Completion.

**6. Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m).** Deferring the release until after Completion leaves the Buyer funding a secured facility it has not yet discharged. The debt should be repaid from the Completion funds with security releases delivered at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and AF approval.

**7. Bonuses (AUD 420,000).** The Seller's funds flow excludes the DD-005 bonuses, and DL 5 confirms the disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. These amounts must appear as a specific line item or be funded by the Seller. Without that, the funds flow silently shifts the cost to the Buyer. Triggered on-costs should be quantified.

**8. Ironquay (AUD 180,000 open per DD-010).** The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. DL 4 confirms there is no evidence of payment or assignment. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction, so do not treat it as settled. Broaden the indemnity and keep the SOW3 cure mechanism.

**9. DD-006 export incident (about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and timestamps).** The Seller calls this "not expected to be material". DL 6 says it is not a confirmed breach and does not say whether notification is required. Our position is to assume neither breach nor notification duty, and not to concede materiality. The Buyer should require log preservation, an investigation, and regular updates. I would also recommend the Buyer consider specific protection for this matter, but that is outside the playbook and should be raised with Amelia Frost.

**10. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** DL 8 says the disclosure does not show whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or ordinary course. The Buyer should review the contracts. The renewals should not be treated automatically as Debt or as a price deduction.

**11. Tax and IP.** The Seller's position that these are "settled under the general regime" is not acceptable. Both remain open. The Buyer should not assume unlimited liability, but should keep them separate from the general regime with their own terms.

**12. Items outside the playbook.** DD-007 (lease notification) and DD-009 (Mossvale assignment restriction) do not state that landlord or Mossvale consent is required for the share sale. These are diligence questions. Ask the Seller to confirm in writing whether consent is needed, and do not assume either way.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Do not accept the Seller's review framework.** Treat every clause as open and disregard the [STANDARD] labels and the "accepted" language.
2. **Counter the limitation package:** 25% / AUD 6.0m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket; 24-month general claims period. Do not offer the 20% or 18-month fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
3. **Separate the title/fundamental regime:** 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket and de minimis, and not subject to the knowledge bar. Require independent title evidence.
4. **Add the fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
5. **Replace the disclosure regime** with specific fair disclosure. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and deemed disclosure. Delete the buyer-knowledge exclusion.
6. **Bluefen:** require effective written consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion.
7. **Riverlark:** repay from Completion funds with security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and AF approval.
8. **Bonuses:** add the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds flow line item, or require Seller funding.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity and keep the SOW3 cure. Verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
10. **DD-006:** require log preservation, investigation and updates. Assume no confirmed breach, notification duty or numeric demand. Do not accept "not material" as a characterisation.
11. **Sandbar:** review the three renewal contracts. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
12. **Tax and IP:** keep open, separate from the general regime, with no assumed unlimited liability.
13. **Diligence confirmations:** ask the Seller to confirm in writing whether lease (DD-007) or Mossvale (DD-009) consent is required for the share sale.

Before the mark-up goes out, Amelia Frost should confirm whether she wants any of the items in section 2 or 9 raised as formal positions.
